PullRequest.Title: agentHost: grant sandbox read access to application contents
PullRequest.Body:

Fixes #346105.

## Summary

Sandboxed canvases need read access to VS Code's application contents, not only its JavaScript application directory. Manually granting the macOS application's `Contents` directory allows the canvas to work with sandboxing enabled.

- Add a memoized `INativeEnvironmentService.appBundleRoot` getter derived from the running host's `appRoot` and product configuration.
- Include this root in Copilot SDK and custom-terminal sandbox default read roots, preserving explicit denies and managed read-only restrictions.
- Keep source/non-packaged layouts at `appRoot` instead of granting an arbitrary ancestor.
- Cover path derivation, sandbox create/resume, and policy composition in focused tests.

| Platform/layout | Default application read root |
| --- | --- |
| macOS | `<application>.app/Contents` |
| Windows | `<installation>` containing `resources\app` |
| Windows with versioned updates | `<installation>` above `<version>\resources\app` |
| Linux | `<installation>` containing `resources/app` |

No new user setting, write permission, or network permission is introduced.

## Validation

- `corepack pnpm run build-fast --client-only` — passed.
- `corepack pnpm run typecheck-client` — passed after restoring the locked dependencies.
- `npm run -s precommit` — passed through the normal commit hook, including oxlint and hygiene checks.
- The following focused test command — **119 passed**:

```powershell
$env:VSCODE_SKIP_PRELAUNCH='1'; & $env:ComSpec /d /c 'scripts\test.bat --run src\vs\platform\environment\test\node\environmentService.test.ts --run src\vs\platform\agentHost\test\node\sandboxConfigForSdk.test.ts --run src\vs\platform\agentHost\test\node\copilotAgentSession.test.ts --grep "EnvironmentService|VS Code sandbox read roots|buildSandboxConfigForSdk|sandbox launch and first turn|per-request sandbox" --reporter dot'
```

The new getter and generated read-only policy were also checked against a versioned Windows Insiders installation. The manually tested macOS permission is documented in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/346105#issuecomment-6902428055. End-to-end canvas launches with the new default have not been verified across macOS, Windows, and Linux.

## Manual verification

1. Run the changed build and enable sandboxing in a Copilot Agent Host chat without manually adding the application directory to read-only paths.
2. Open a plugin canvas and verify that it opens while sandboxing remains enabled.
3. Repeat with a resumed chat and on each desktop OS, including a versioned Windows installation.

Scenarios.Scenario: Create or resume a Copilot Agent Host session with SDK sandboxing enabled, then apply later sandbox configuration changes.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Session configuration is built before the SDK create/resume RPC; the sandbox configuration is included in that existing RPC and is applied again through the existing options.update RPC during finalization. Later relevant config changes pass through the existing sequencer and await options.update only when serialized configuration differs.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: SDK createSession/resumeSession carries sandboxConfig containing one additional readonly path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One existing open call per create/resume attempt; fallback/retry counts are unchanged by the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same open RPC already carried sandboxConfig with session, shell-init, attachment, and plugin roots; it lacked the application root.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The existing SDK open call is on the session-launch critical path; the diff only adds one bounded string to its payload.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: session.rpc.options.update applies sandboxConfig after launch or on a changed effective policy.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One existing post-open apply per launch and one per distinct serialized config change; unchanged updates are coalesced by _appliedConfig.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same update already transmitted sandboxConfig; the readonly path array had one fewer constant entry.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The existing post-open update is awaited during finalization or config application; the diff changes payload size by one path but not call count.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One added application-root string per sandbox configuration, independent of application file count, attachment count, plugin count, history size, or workspace size.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Launch operations follow the existing session launch sequence. Runtime configuration mutations are serialized by _configSequencer; the diff introduces no parallel RPCs or burst.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: appBundleRoot is memoized on first access. _appliedConfig stores the serialized effective configuration and suppresses unchanged options.update calls; managed readonly policy can omit all host-generated extra roots. No new cache key or negative-cache state is introduced.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from tracing getLaunchConfig/_computeConfig through launch and _updateConfig: the changed behavior alters only the existing configuration payload and no boundary cardinality.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact SDK serialization and runtime policy-compilation duration is not measured, but the increment is one path string and cannot scale with installation contents because no traversal is performed here.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The diff adds bounded constant-size serialization to existing, deduplicated IPC without increasing boundary calls or concurrency.

Scenarios.Scenario: Wrap or preflight a command through the Agent Host custom terminal sandbox.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: On first use or policy/command invalidation, wrapCommand awaits sandbox JSON regeneration before returning a wrapped command. checkFileAccess independently resolves effective filesystem paths before returning its preflight decision.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Canonicalize the application root with fileService.realpath while resolving allow-read paths.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One additional realpath per sandbox JSON regeneration and per checkFileAccess policy resolution; it is batched with existing root resolutions and does not recurse into the directory.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Existing session, runtime, workspace, configured, and command roots were canonicalized; the application installation root was not.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Awaited by policy generation/access preflight, but adds only one local metadata lookup at constant cardinality.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Overwrite the terminal sandbox JSON policy file.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One existing write per first use or invalidating refresh; unchanged commands reuse the cached path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same file was already serialized and written with all other effective roots.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Awaited before command wrapping; payload grows by one path (or original plus canonical path for a symlink).

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One additional host read root per generated/access-check policy. Cost scales with sandbox regenerations or access checks, not with the number of files beneath the application root.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: All effective paths in one policy are canonicalized with Promise.all, so the new realpath joins the existing batch. The engine caches the generated config path between unchanged commands; the diff adds no scheduler, queue, or new command-level parallelism.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The environment getter is memoized. TerminalSandboxEngine reuses _sandboxConfigPath until force refresh or root/settings/command inputs require regeneration; canonicalized roots themselves are not cached, so the new root adds one realpath per regeneration or access check.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence that one filesystem operation is added on regeneration/access checks; high confidence that it remains constant-cardinality and joins an existing parallel resolution batch.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Filesystem latency varies, but the added operation is one local realpath against the installed application directory and no evidence shows traversal, fan-out, or a remote/network path in this scenario.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The single bounded metadata lookup is a micro-cost, while config caching prevents unconditional per-command repetition and no directory contents are scanned.

Scenarios.Scenario: Resolve the native application bundle root for sandbox policy composition.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The first sandbox policy computation reads appBundleRoot and performs synchronous path parsing; subsequent reads return the memoized value. This work occurs before the existing sandbox RPC or terminal-policy generation.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Fixed number of dirname/basename/parse operations over one short installation path.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous one-time getter evaluation per environment-service instance; no spawned work or fan-out.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: @memoize retains the computed string for the environment-service lifetime. Source/non-built layouts return the already memoized appRoot.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from the getter and getAppBundleRoot implementation.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: None material: the helper performs no filesystem, IPC, network, subprocess, or database operation.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. This is bounded one-time CPU work with no expensive boundary.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass across all 10 changed files. Traced SDK create/resume/update, custom-terminal command wrapping and access checks, and environment path derivation. The PR adds one memoized path and one constant-size policy entry; it does not add scalable traversal, boundary fan-out, concurrency, retention, or materially larger serialization. No findings were submitted.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
